headline: Stocks Enter Friday on Firm Footing After Broad Thursday Rally
body_html:
Wall Street heads into Friday's open with momentum at its back. Thursday's session closed on a constructive note, with 365 stocks advancing against 174 declining across our 544-name universe — a decidedly lopsided outcome in favor of buyers. Homebuilders led all sectors with a gain of 4.09%, followed by Consumer names up 2.60% and Software up 2.51%. Healthcare added nearly 2%, while Materials and Industrials posted modest positive closes. The only drags came from Semiconductors, off 0.67%, and Energy, which shed 1.01% even as oil prices remain on track for a weekly gain tied to Middle East supply concerns.

The day's sharpest individual moves offered a mixed picture beneath the surface. Trade Desk surged 7.80%, AppFolio climbed 7.59%, and Roblox jumped 7.55% to round out a spirited session for internet and software names. On the other end, Vicor Corporation tumbled 10.36% and Semtech dropped 10.01%, keeping the semiconductor space under pressure and underscoring the sector's continued vulnerability as investors reassess hardware demand.

Looking ahead to the Friday open, macro watchers will track oil's trajectory and any fresh developments out of the Middle East. Fed Governor Warsh's remarks overnight — characterizing artificial intelligence's economic path as ultimately wealth-creating but near-term turbulent — may add texture to conversations around rate policy and tech valuations. With no obvious domestic catalyst to reset the mood, the burden falls on geopolitics and any pre-weekend positioning flows.

briefs.headline: Fed's Warsh Flags a Rocky Road Ahead for AI's Economic Impact
briefs.body: Federal Reserve Governor Warsh acknowledged overnight that artificial intelligence will prove highly beneficial to national wealth over time, but cautioned investors not to expect a smooth ride. He described the near-term trajectory as likely to be quite turbulent, a framing that may temper enthusiasm for high-multiple technology names heading into Friday's session.

briefs.headline: Oil Steadies Near Weekly Highs as Middle East Tensions Persist
briefs.body: Crude prices eased slightly in overnight trading but remain positioned for a weekly gain, with institutional focus fixed on potential supply disruptions stemming from ongoing Middle East conflict. Separately, India moved to raise its windfall tax on petrol while trimming the levy on diesel, a policy shift that could influence regional refining margins and freight economics.

briefs.headline: Hezbollah Claims Ownership of Confiscated Explosives Linked to Israel Plot
briefs.body: The militant group publicly acknowledged that explosives seized by Lebanese authorities belonged to its operatives and were intended for use against Israeli targets. U.S. Secretary of State Rubio separately urged Lebanese officials not to return the material to Hezbollah, adding diplomatic pressure to an already volatile security situation in the region.

briefs.headline: Global Shipping Patterns Shift as Bunker Buyers Reroute Around Conflict Zones
briefs.body: Industry executives told reporters this week that the prolonged Middle East conflict is meaningfully reshaping how shippers purchase bunker fuel, with traditional procurement routes being abandoned in favor of alternatives that avoid high-risk corridors. The shift adds logistical cost and complexity for carriers operating in the region.

briefs.headline: Bank of England Governor Sees Limited Wage-Price Spiral So Far
briefs.body: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey offered a cautiously reassuring read on inflation dynamics Thursday, noting that second-round price pressures — the mechanism through which initial cost shocks feed into wages and then back into prices — have remained relatively muted. Markets interpreted his remarks as consistent with a gradual easing path for U.K. monetary policy.

briefs.headline: KFC Switches Its U.S. Fountain Beverage Partner for First Time in Decades
briefs.body: The fast-food chain announced it will replace its longstanding U.S. beverage supplier with Coca-Cola across its domestic restaurant network, ending an arrangement that had been in place for many years. The deal marks a notable shift in quick-service restaurant pouring rights and signals competitive intensity in the fountain beverage distribution market.
